claims.text: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging implicitly creates a log scope with SpanId, TraceId and ParentId of the current Activity (LoggerFactoryOptions.ActivityTrackingOptions); the default ASP.NET Core/generic host turns these three on.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs 'Logging in .NET and ASP.NET Core' § 'Automatically log scope with SpanId, TraceId, and ParentId'; refs/aspnetcore-docs fundamentals/logging/index.md

claims.text: The JSON console formatter writes a line's open scopes in a 'Scopes' array only when JsonConsoleFormatterOptions.IncludeScopes is true; each scope with name–value state appears as an object with 'Message' and its names.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Console log formatting' (JsonConsoleFormatter, IncludeScopes); don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/json-logs.txt lines 19-35

claims.text: At stage-3 api, notifications, payments and fake-gateway set Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__IncludeScopes: "true" next to Logging__Console__FormatterName: "json" in docker-compose.yml; no log call changed.
At stage-3 RequestLoggingMiddleware logs '{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms', and its JSON line carries a Scopes entry with SpanId, TraceId and ParentId.

Alloy's loki.process stage.json evaluates JMESPath 'Scopes[?TraceId] | [0].TraceId' (first Scopes entry that has TraceId); stage.structured_metadata with an empty value uses the extracted value of the same name as the line's structured metadata.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Alloy docs 'loki.process' (stage.json expressions, stage.structured_metadata values: empty value = same-name extracted key)

claims.text: config.alloy's comment at stage-3 (lines 29-33) states that a line with no trace id passes through as it is; the lesson attributes this to the comment, not to Alloy's documentation.
Loki structured metadata is name–value data stored with each log line; it is not part of the stream's labels and is not indexed.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs 'What is structured metadata'

claims.text: In Loki each unique set of label values defines a separate stream, and labels are what Loki indexes; a label with one value per request would create one stream per request.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs 'Understand labels' / 'Cardinality'; 'Label best practices'

claims.text: A LogQL label filter expression after the stream selector, such as | trace_id="<id>", matches structured metadata; != "text" is a line filter that drops lines containing the text.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs 'Log queries' (label filter expressions, line filter expressions); 'Query structured metadata'

claims.text: logs-for-trace.sh lines 25-31 build {service=~"api|payments|notifications"} | trace_id="$id" with != line filters that drop the EF Core and HttpClient lines written inside the same trace; $id comes from trace_id "$traceparent" (line 23).
The rest of logs-for-trace.sh sends the query to Loki's /loki/api/v1/query_range with only a start time, and prints each line's service and Message sorted by time.
Captured output at stage-3: -> 202, the logql> line, then four lines: api POST refund responded 202; notifications refund requested email; payments refund done; notifications order refunded email.

datasources.yml (sets up Grafana's data sources) at stage-3 gives the Loki data source a derived field TraceId with matcherType label, matcherRegex trace_id, datasourceUid tempo, urlDisplayLabel 'Open the trace'.

In Grafana's Loki data source, a derived field of type Label matches a label key of each line (Loki returns structured metadata among a line's labels); as an internal link with a target data source, it opens the value as a query there, here a Tempo trace.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs 'Loki data source' § 'Derived fields' (Type: Label, internal link)

claims.text: Alloy reads each container's output through the Docker socket and forwards it, labelled with service, to Loki; from stage-3 it goes through loki.process "trace_ids" before loki.write.
Prometheus metric labels split a metric into separate time series, one per distinct label set, so a per-request label value would create a series per request.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs 'Data model' (time series identified by metric name and labels); 'Naming' (label cardinality caution)
